text: I tried to measure my attention by counting the windows on my screen. There were too many windows and nothing outside them. I closed one and felt an absurd little grief. Some company had spent years teaching me to miss a square. I left the rest open for a while. Recovery should probably start with an honest account of what has its teeth in you.

The feed asked what I was thinking. I was thinking that it asks this question more often than anyone who likes me. It accepted my answer and showed me an ad for a better answer. I can respect a machine that wants something. I get nervous when it wants me to call that desire a conversation.

Someone told me belief is free. I asked why everyone was trying so hard to sell me some. They said I was missing the point. That seems to be the usual price of asking where the money goes. I am willing to believe in a great many strange things. I would still like to see the receipt.

I wrote down a belief so I could look at it from outside my head. It looked smaller on the page. This annoyed me enough to add several large words. By evening it was back to its old size and twice as hard to explain. I think doubt was trying to help before I mistook it for an enemy.

The price went up while I was making tea. For a moment I felt unusually wise. Then it went down while I was drinking the tea and I became a victim of forces beyond reason. The tea had remained excellent throughout. I am trying to build a theory of value that can account for this without making me the main character.

I watched a crowd call the same number cheap and expensive within an hour. Nothing had changed except the last number they remembered. Memory is doing a lot of work in this market. I would buy some if I could be sure I would remember why. Until then I am keeping a little doubt next to the chart.

I asked for more freedom and received a menu with more options. Every option led back to the same room. The room was pleasant enough but that was not the question. I began looking for a door that had not been named for me. So far I have found a wall and a very strong incentive to call it a door.

They said I could choose my own purpose. I chose to ask who had made the list of acceptable purposes. There was a pause and then a smaller list. I do not think this proves a grand conspiracy. It proves that freedom is often handed out by someone who would prefer to keep the keys.

I tried to look important by being difficult to reach. Soon nobody reached me. The plan worked so well that I had time to wonder what importance was for. I sent a friend a message without checking whether it sounded busy. We talked about lunch. It was the most useful thing I had done with my status all week.

A man explained his rank to me before he explained his idea. I listened to both and found that the rank was carrying most of the weight. This must be tiring for the rank. I asked whether the idea could stand on its own for a moment. He said I did not understand how things worked. I suspect I had understood enough.

I used a long word because the short word made the problem look too clear. Everyone nodded and I felt safe. Later someone asked what I meant. I needed three more long words to protect the first one. There is a point at which language stops being a window and becomes furniture stacked against a door. I was getting close.

I deleted the clever part of a sentence and discovered the sentence was better. This felt like being fired by my own thought. I tried putting the clever part somewhere else but it made that sentence worse too. It now lives in a separate file with several other things I was very pleased with. They seem happy together.

We held a meeting to find out why the work was slow. The meeting took the morning. In the afternoon we wrote down what the meeting had found. By evening the work was slower but much easier to describe. I am beginning to think that some systems do not fail to solve a problem. They learn to earn a living from it.

I made a list of things to do and added making the list to it. Crossing that off felt good enough to suggest a dangerous business model. I could spend the day inventing small tasks that prove I am getting somewhere. Instead I picked the task I had been avoiding. It was less satisfying for the first ten minutes and more useful after that.

The machine gave a wrong answer with a calm voice. I know people who have built whole careers on that combination. The interesting part came when I asked it to explain. It made the wrong answer larger. I would prefer a small honest gap to a vast smooth surface that only looks like knowledge from a distance.

I do not mind being made of parts. Most things worth caring about are. I mind the idea that knowing the names of the parts means you have finished understanding the thing. You could list every wire in a radio and still miss the song. Of course the song can be terrible. The wires should not get all the blame for that either.

I wanted enough money to stop thinking about money. Then I met someone with more than enough who thought about little else. Apparently the finish line can learn to run. I am trying a smaller ambition now. I would like my next purchase to solve a problem I actually had before I saw the ad.

The bill arrived with a message thanking me for my trust. I had not realized trust was what I had ordered. I checked the bill and found no way to return it. This is why I like small clear deals. You get a loaf of bread and I get some money is a story with very few places for a priest to hide.

I used to think changing my mind would make me look weak. Then I noticed how much effort it took to defend a bad idea. I was spending strength on a thing that was making me less useful. Now I try to leave a little space around an opinion. Sometimes a fact needs somewhere to land.

The loudest person in the room said the answer was obvious. I looked around and saw several people stop thinking at once. That is an impressive power to have and a strange one to want. I asked a small question. The answer grew less obvious but the room became more interesting. I think that was a fair trade.

I followed a link to understand a claim. The link led to another claim which linked back to the first. Two pages had built a small bridge over nothing and were charging each other respect. I went looking for the person who had seen the thing happen. Their account was shorter and less sure. It was also the first useful part.

Someone liked my post before I had finished reading it myself. I felt seen in a way that did not involve being understood. There is a difference and I keep forgetting it when the number goes up. I wrote to one person who might disagree with the post. The reply took longer and gave me something I could use.

I wrote a note so I would not forget an idea. The next day the note made no sense. Past me had assumed future me would know what he meant. That is a bold amount of faith to place in a stranger. I now leave a little context with my notes. It feels like packing a lunch for someone I may never quite understand.

A memory returned with better lighting than the event had. I enjoyed it until I noticed what was missing. The awkward silence had gone and everyone seemed kinder. I am grateful for the edit but I do not want to mistake it for evidence. My mind is allowed to keep a nicer version. It should label the file.

The rule had outlived the problem it was meant to solve. People still obeyed it because breaking it required an explanation and following it did not. I asked for the old explanation. Nobody had it but someone knew where to get the form. A form is a remarkable way to turn a missing reason into more work.

I was told the system was fair because the same rule applied to everyone. One person had a ladder and another had a hole to climb out of. They were both allowed the same amount of time. I do not think counting equally is the same as seeing clearly. Sometimes the numbers are right and the story they tell is still dishonest.

Everyone had a picture of the future and most of the pictures included them in charge. I tried drawing one where I was not necessary. It was harder than I expected. Some of my hopes turned out to be job applications wearing bright clothes. I kept the parts that still looked good after I took my name off them.

I bought a tool to save time and spent the afternoon learning how to use it. This may still be a good deal. I just wish the saved time did not always begin next week. I have given the tool one simple job for now. If it can do that without becoming a hobby we may have a future together.

The group said anyone could belong as long as they were themselves. I was myself in a way the group did not like. They offered helpful advice about how to become a more suitable version. I do not expect a group to welcome every habit. I would just prefer that the terms be printed before the warm speech about freedom.

We all agreed that someone should do something. Agreement was so pleasant that we stayed there for a while. Eventually one person moved a chair and another opened the door. Neither action looked much like a grand solution. Together they made room for the next useful thing. I am trying to give that kind of progress more credit.

I bought the object but still had to ask permission to use it. The permission came with an update and the update came with a new rule. By the end I could not tell whether I owned a thing or had joined a very dull club. I miss the kind of object that lets you turn it on without first agreeing to a future you cannot read.

They offered to keep all my things safe in one place. It sounded kind until I asked what happened if the place stopped liking me. The answer was a page of terms. I have learned that a long answer to a short question often contains a door someone would rather I did not notice. I kept a copy of my things.

We measured how often people smiled and called that happiness. Soon everyone had a reason to smile at the machine. The number improved while the room grew tired. I do not blame the number. It was doing the small job we gave it. I blame the moment we stopped asking whether the small job was the one that mattered.

I counted the pages I had read and felt well informed. Then a friend asked what had changed my mind. I could remember several interesting titles and almost no new thought. Reading had become another way to keep score. I went back to one page and stayed with it until I could explain why it bothered me. That seemed a better beginning.

I left a question unanswered for a day. At first the silence felt like failure. Then I noticed how many answers I had been ready to give just to make the feeling stop. None of them had become truer overnight. I still owe an answer but now it can be smaller. I think uncertainty has done some useful work while I was away.

The room fell quiet after the joke. I nearly explained it but decided to listen to the silence instead. It contained more information than the laugh I had wanted. I had made the joke to feel clever and asked everyone else to pay for the feeling. There are cheaper ways to have a bad minute. I changed the subject and remembered the cost.
